options: Still bill 99213-95-25 + 20610 — the visits were at different times
The E/M is part of the decision for the procedure — it is NOT separately billable; bill only 20610
Bill 99214 instead
questions.explanation: If the E/M's sole purpose was deciding to do the procedure, it is included in the procedure's global work — modifier 25 requires the E/M to be significant AND separately identifiable beyond the decision to perform the procedure.
questions.hint: Was there E/M work beyond 'should I do this injection'?

questions.q: A scrubber flags 99213-95-25 (POS 02) + 20610 (POS 11). The biller's first check should be:
options: Delete the telehealth line — same-day always bundles
Verify documentation supports a significant, separately identifiable E/M distinct from the procedure decision, with separate notes for each encounter
Change POS 02 to POS 11 to avoid the flag
Add modifier 59 to the injection
questions.explanation: Same-day E/M + procedure with 25 is legitimate but heavily audited. The defense is documentation: two distinct encounter notes showing the E/M addressed issues beyond the procedure decision. Never change POS to dodge a flag — that is misrepresentation.
questions.hint: What proves the 25 was earned?

questions.q: Which modifier combination is NEVER correct?
questions.explanation: Modifier 59 is for procedures only — it NEVER goes on an E/M code. 99213-59 is always wrong. (25 goes on E/M; 59/X-modifiers go on procedures; 95 identifies telehealth and can combine with 25.)
questions.hint: Which code type can never take modifier 59?

title: Originating Site Facility Fee: Q3014
description: The patient is at a clinic, the doctor is remote — the originating site bills Q3014 for hosting the telehealth visit.

questions.q: A rural clinic hosts a telehealth visit: patient at the clinic, specialist video-calls in from 200 miles away. The clinic (originating site) bills what?
options: 99213-95 — the clinic bills the visit
Q3014 — telehealth originating site facility fee
POS 02 with the E/M code
Nothing — only the distant provider bills
questions.explanation: Q3014 is the originating-site facility fee — it compensates the site hosting the patient (room, equipment, staff). The distant-site provider bills the E/M with 95/POS 02; the originating site bills Q3014.
questions.hint: There is a specific HCPCS code for the hosting site.

questions.q: Can the patient's home be an originating site for Q3014?
options: Yes — always

Under traditional Medicare rules, the home was generally NOT a valid originating site for Q3014 (originating sites were specific facility types); pandemic-era flexibilities expanded this and rules continue to evolve — verify current CMS guidance
No — Q3014 is only for hospitals
Only for audio-only visits
questions.explanation: Traditional originating-site rules limited Q3014 to facilities (offices, hospitals, rural clinics, etc.) — not the patient's home. COVID flexibilities changed this temporarily; the rules have been extended/modified since. This is a must-verify-current-guidance area.
questions.hint: Were homes originally on the originating-site list?

questions.q: The originating site bills Q3014 and ALSO bills 99213 for the same visit. What is wrong?
options: Nothing — both are billable
Double billing: the originating site did not provide the E/M service — the distant provider did. The originating site bills ONLY Q3014; the distant provider bills the E/M
Q3014 replaces the need for modifier 95
The originating site should bill with POS 02
questions.explanation: Only the distant-site provider bills the E/M. The originating site's role is hosting — compensated via Q3014 only. Billing the E/M from the originating site duplicates the distant provider's claim.
questions.hint: Who actually performed the medical service?

questions.q: Q3014 pays approximately $30. A clinic hosts 40 telehealth visits/month. What is the annual facility-fee revenue, and why does it matter?
options: $1,200/year — negligible
$14,400/year (40 x $30 x 12) — meaningful revenue that funds the telehealth room, equipment, and staff time; clinics that do not bill Q3014 leave money on the table
$30 total — Q3014 is once per year
Q3014 is not payable, so $0
questions.explanation: 40 x $30 x 12 = $14,400/year. For rural/small clinics, the originating-site fee is what makes hosting telehealth financially viable — yet many eligible sites never bill it.
questions.hint: Do the multiplication.
